domain_overview.domain_summary: The industrial component domain encompasses various parts and devices used in industrial applications, focusing on their design, function, and integration. It ensures the efficient operation of machinery and systems.
domain_overview.sub_domain_summary: Electrical equipment within the industrial component domain includes devices that control, distribute, and convert electrical power. These components are critical for the safe and efficient operation of industrial systems.
domain_overview.functional_purpose: Power relays are used to control high-power circuits with low-power signals, providing isolation and protection for control circuits. They play a crucial role in automation and safety systems.
domain_overview.system_boundaries: Power relays interact with control systems, power distribution networks, and safety systems. Their boundaries include the electrical circuits they control and the physical enclosures they are housed in.

primary.name: Power Relay
primary.description: A device that opens or closes electrical contacts to control the flow of electricity in a circuit.

supporting_infrastructure.name: Relay Socket
supporting_infrastructure.description: A base that holds the relay and connects it to the circuit.

supporting_infrastructure.name: Control Circuit
supporting_infrastructure.description: The circuit that sends signals to the relay to control its operation.

control_and_monitoring.name: Relay Controller
control_and_monitoring.description: A device or system that sends control signals to the relay.

control_and_monitoring.name: Monitoring System
control_and_monitoring.description: A system that monitors the status and performance of the relay.

safety_and_protection.name: Circuit Breaker
safety_and_protection.description: A device that automatically interrupts the flow of electricity in case of a fault.

safety_and_protection.name: Surge Protector
safety_and_protection.description: A device that protects the relay and circuit from voltage spikes.

governance.name: IEC 61810
governance.description: International standard for electromechanical elementary relays.

governance.name: UL Certification
governance.description: Certification indicating compliance with safety standards.

terminology.functional_role: Central component for controlling electrical circuits in industrial systems.

terminology.definition: A base that holds the relay and connects it to the circuit.
terminology.functional_role: Provides a secure and reliable connection for the relay.

terminology.definition: A circuit that sends signals to the relay to control its operation.
terminology.functional_role: Enables the relay to perform its switching function.

terminology.definition: A device or system that sends control signals to the relay.
terminology.functional_role: Manages the operation of the relay based on input signals.

terminology.definition: A system that monitors the status and performance of the relay.
terminology.functional_role: Ensures the relay operates within specified parameters.

terminology.definition: A device that automatically interrupts the flow of electricity in case of a fault.
terminology.functional_role: Protects the relay and circuit from damage due to overloads.

terminology.definition: A device that protects the relay and circuit from voltage spikes.
terminology.functional_role: Prevents damage to the relay from electrical surges.

terminology.definition: International standard for electromechanical elementary relays.
terminology.functional_role: Ensures relays meet international safety and performance standards.

terminology.definition: Certification indicating compliance with safety standards.
terminology.functional_role: Provides assurance of relay safety and reliability.

terminology.definition: The voltage required to energize the relay coil.
terminology.functional_role: Determines the control signal needed to operate the relay.

terminology.definition: The maximum current the relay contacts can carry.
terminology.functional_role: Specifies the load capacity of the relay.

terminology.definition: The resistance between electrically isolated parts of the relay.
The time it takes for the relay to switch from one state to another.
terminology.functional_role: Affects the speed of operation in control systems.

terminology.definition: The number of times the relay can operate before failure.
terminology.functional_role: Indicates the durability and lifespan of the relay.

terminology.definition: The resistance across the closed contacts of the relay.
terminology.functional_role: Affects the efficiency and performance of the relay.

workflows: Step 1: Control circuit sends a signal to the relay coil.
Step 2: Relay coil energizes, creating a magnetic field.
Step 3: Magnetic field moves the relay armature, closing or opening contacts.
Step 4: Electrical circuit is completed or interrupted, controlling the load.
Step 5: Monitoring system checks relay status and performance.
operational_logic.energy_flow: Control circuit sends a low-power signal to the relay coil, which controls a high-power circuit by opening or closing contacts.
failure_conditions: Coil burnout due to excessive voltage.
Contact welding due to high current.
compliance_constraints: Must have UL certification for safety.
Must meet RoHS compliance for environmental safety.

invariants.description: Every power relay must have a specified coil voltage.
Every power relay must comply with IEC 61810 standards.
Every power relay must be protected by a circuit breaker.
Every power relay must be monitored by a monitoring system.
Every power relay must have a specified contact current rating.
